description:
## Summary

For agent-authored Radicle state to be durable and verifiable, project-controlled node infrastructure must hold it. Deliver a persistent Radicle node — and/or a project-controlled always-on seed — on the operator's key-holding device and/or host, with a declared seeding policy under which the Tesserine working repositories and their collaboration state (including issues and patches authored by per-session contributor identities) verifiably replicate.

Part of: tesserine/groundwork#538 (execution-boundary enablement for the Radicle-native replacement). Kin: tesserine/commons#109 (repository homes migrating to Radicle), #64 (the connector-era forge-credential separation this topology supersedes for Radicle operations).

## Scope

- Host provisioning for the Radicle node/seed (service lifecycle, reboot survival)
- The declared seeding policy and its durable home
- Custody runbook (delegate identity boundary)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Radicle 1.9.x node runs persistently on the designated host(s) and survives reboot under ordinary service lifecycle.
- [ ] The operator's delegate identity is created and held only on its key-holding device; provisioning never copies key material off that device; `RAD_PASSPHRASE`-in-environment is not used as a custody mechanism.
- [ ] A declared seeding policy names which node(s) seed the working repositories and with what scope (followed vs all), such that state authored by per-session contributor DIDs replicates to project-controlled node(s); the policy lives at a durable home that Groundwork's verification mechanics can consult.
- [ ] Replication is demonstrated: state authored by a non-delegate peer reaches the declared node(s), observed by replication read-back.
- [ ] A runbook documents provisioning and the custody boundary.

## Dependencies

None — operator-led host enablement; may proceed independently of the ADR gate (it also serves tesserine/commons#109). Consumed by tesserine/groundwork#538's topology, end-to-end, and terminal units.
